headline: LOCAL STAR COMMONS opens a contribution-governed movement for useful neighborhood infrastructure
subhead: A desktop local-compute hub and five quality-of-life companions enter an off-chain founding commons centered on a 25-mile El Segundo test area.
disclosure: Official PointCast Press Wire filing for LOCAL STAR COMMONS. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
summary: LOCAL STAR COMMONS publishes a six-object quality-of-life system, a contribution-based founding constitution, and a directional 25-mile El Segundo pilot study with explicit off-chain and no-token boundaries.
body: LOCAL STAR, AIR, WATER, LIGHT, CARE, and POWER form one related local-first product family. LOCAL STAR combines the visual language of a small satellite dish with desktop compute, sensing, and neighborhood mesh capability. The five companion directions extend that hub into quieter environmental awareness, earlier household signals, privacy-first check-ins, neighbor-scale communication, and practical resilience.

The Commons places those objects inside an off-chain founding constitution. Product, Field, Care, Stewardship, and Story circles can move proposals through signal, shape, review, vote, field, and learn. The first three proposals call for a public First Field Table, a 25-mile El Segundo pilot ring, and an Open Repair Ledger. Participation grows through visible contribution rather than a purchased token.

The pilot map considers the aerospace, aviation, logistics, manufacturing, media, health, education, civic, hospitality, and coastal-resilience worlds surrounding El Segundo. It is a directional test-area study, not a claim of partnerships, installations, permits, procurement, or municipal affiliation.

DAO in this release means a public coordination prototype, not a legal entity or autonomous on-chain organization. There is no token, treasury, fundraising, binding shared vote, Mainnet action, certified hardware program, satellite service, emergency system, or operating physical mesh. Site signals are stored only on the visitor's device. PointCast distributes the release through a canonical route, machine JSON, Block 0490, feeds, Press Wire, and one clearly labeled house-ad creative.

kicker: 25-MILE HORIZON · 24 MONTHS · $295 FIRST LINK · LOCAL FIRST
headline: Network El Segundo publishes a cash-floor, two-year plan for a useful community mesh
subhead: Three consented rooftops, three directional paths, donated compute, and local-only sites establish the first honest mesh before internet transit enters the design.
disclosure: Official PointCast Press Wire filing for Network El Segundo. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
summary: Mesh Commons translates NYC Mesh’s line-of-sight-first community model into a two-year El Segundo plan with a $295–$395 first-link floor, a redundant three-roof starting shape, and nine local-only services.
body: Network El Segundo has published Mesh Commons, a practical two-year plan for a community-owned local network centered in El Segundo. The least-expensive honest starting shape is three consented rooftops, three directional radio paths, one donated service computer, and local services that remain useful when an upstream internet gateway is unavailable.

The equipment floor for the first measured two-roof link is $295–$395. It assumes two $65-class outdoor radios, a small router, outdoor cable, surge and grounding allowances, a light mounting contingency, donated compute, volunteer labor, and legal roof access. The first redundant triangle is budgeted at $950–$1,500; the year-one hardware floor is $3,000–$5,000; and the 24-month floor is $9,500–$15,000 for 12–20 roofs and four to six hubs. Professional roof, electrical, engineering, permitting, insurance, tower-rent, unusual-mount, and internet-backhaul costs are excluded.

The workflow borrows directly from NYC Mesh’s public documentation: potential nodes enter a map, panoramic roof views establish line-of-sight candidates, equipment is purchased after viability, directional client radios connect into hubs, and mature clusters retain at least two uplinks. The governance direction also adopts the Network Commons freedoms to use the network, understand it, offer services, and extend it to others under the same conditions.

The first service cabinet includes hello.mesh, map.mesh, play.mesh, bbs.mesh, radio.mesh, library.mesh, drop.mesh, garden.mesh, and atelier.mesh. Local access has no mandatory monthly price; the plan suggests $5–$20 or volunteer time and excludes browsing-history, message-content, open-microphone, public-home-address, and location-history collection.

The 25-mile radius is a planning horizon for linked clusters, not a promise of blanket coverage. Any 15–25 mile proof link remains contingent on site permission, safe mounting, rooftop height, spectrum conditions, Fresnel clearance, and engineering review. Mesh Commons is a planning artifact, not an active physical mesh, internet service offering, emergency network, certified design, site survey, municipal program, or authorization to install.

kicker: 8 OBJECTS · 4 SIGNALS · 24 CONCEPT NODES · SIGNED MH
headline: Network El Segundo opens a local signal field kit for neighbor-scale communication
subhead: Beams, window lights, quiet chimes, touch signals, paper cards, and a zero-fire Microburst share one four-signal protocol across a diagrammatic El Segundo rollout.
disclosure: Official PointCast Press Wire filing for Network El Segundo. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
productLabel: Open the Local Signal Field Kit
summary: The signed MH Local Signal Field Kit publishes eight neighbor-scale communication concepts, a four-signal protocol, and a three-phase El Segundo mesh rehearsal with explicit safety and privacy boundaries.
body: Network El Segundo has published eight product briefs for local communication: Porch Beam, Window Flag, Corner Chime, Microburst, Hush Pebble, Roof Ripple, Mesh Post, and Field Cards. They carry the same four shared meanings—hello, meet, need a hand, and all clear—through light, quiet sound, touch, reflection, and a short-lived local relay.

The interactive map sketches a deliberately small rollout. Phase one is an eight-node porch loop around local parks, Main Street, Smoky Hollow, the Civic Center, and one transit edge. Phase two expands to a sixteen-node cross-town thread. Phase three is a twenty-four-node, one-hour dusk rehearsal from the Pacific edge toward the eastside campus and Douglas. The map is diagrammatic rather than navigational, and each host is opt-in.

Microburst provides the emotional shape of a mini firework without pyrotechnics: a rechargeable ten-second fan of LEDs and reflective fins with no flame, smoke, explosive material, projectile, or debris. The wider field kit likewise excludes skyward lasers, emergency imitation, surveillance, open microphones, location history, and continuous sound.

The release is signed MH and is public as both a regular interactive site and a canonical PointCast route with companion JSON, Block 0488, JSON and RSS feed distribution, Press Wire, and a fifth creative in the Network El Segundo house campaign. It is a concept system, not certified hardware, emergency infrastructure, a municipal program, or an active physical mesh.

kicker: 100 LIGHTS · LIVE COUNT · ONE FREE SIGNATURE
headline: Network El Segundo turns its first 100 verified wallets into a living public signal
subhead: Each free Kukai wallet-control signature now illuminates one position in a privacy-preserving artwork distributed through PointCast and its reciprocal house-ad network.
disclosure: Official PointCast Press Wire filing for Network El Segundo. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
summary: The First 100 Signal converts Network El Segundo's verified Tezos wallet count into a living 100-light composition while keeping public wallet addresses out of the visual field.
body: Network El Segundo has added The First 100 Signal, a living public artwork driven by its deduplicated verified-wallet roster. The composition contains one hundred light positions. Each unique Tezos Mainnet wallet verified through the free Kukai-compatible message flow turns on one position, and the field refreshes from the public count every thirty seconds.

The visual publishes collective proof without publishing wallet addresses. The artwork receives only the number of verified participants; it does not display an address, email, profile, page-view estimate, or visitor identifier. The same count remains independently inspectable through the public participant API.

PointCast now carries the Signal through its canonical Network El Segundo desk, JSON release packet, JSON and RSS feeds, sitewide first-100 strip, Press Wire, and three contextual house ads. Reciprocal publishers that pin the Network El Segundo campaign receive the updated creative language through the portable Open Ad Network.

Joining still costs zero tez and requires no purchase, mint, funding, or transaction. The signature proves wallet control only. Art-sale settlement, the proposed 50 percent participant distribution rule, payout automation, token mechanics, yield, and any promised return remain inactive prototypes.

headline: The Holders’ Cut opens a 44-plate public preview for an unlimited Tezos edition
subhead: A recovered image archive, transparent 10-tez mint model, and proposed 50% holder pool arrive as a public pre-launch artifact while Mainnet minting remains inactive.
disclosure: Official PointCast Press Wire filing for The Holders’ Cut. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
summary: The Holders’ Cut presents 44 recovered image plates as an open-ended public edition concept with a 10-tez unit price, a proposed holder allocation, and an explicit pre-Mainnet launch boundary.
body: The Holders’ Cut is public as a 44-image web archive and pre-launch edition proposal. The site uses the complete supplied archive rather than a single hero image, with a responsive image field, individual plate inspection, a quantity receipt, and a transparent accounting calculator.

The proposed edition is unlimited and priced at 10 tez per mint. The accompanying holder-pool proposal allocates 50 percent of defined net primary proceeds to eligible holder wallets at published Tezos snapshots, with the remaining definitions, costs, eligibility rules, and claim method still subject to contract and offering review.

This release does not originate a Tezos contract, connect a wallet, request a signature, move tez, mint a token, or promise a financial return. The Mainnet action is visibly locked on the public site. A live edition would require a separately reviewed contract, published payout rules, explicit wallet approval, and applied-operation verification.

PointCast is distributing the public preview through its owned Press Wire and a clearly labeled house ad. Rally carries the same contextual creative in its footer through the portable PointCast Open Ad Network, with aggregate impression and click counts and no cross-site visitor profile, cookie, wallet identifier, or behavioral targeting.

kicker: FIRST 100 WALLETS · FREE SIGNATURE · PUBLIC COUNTER
headline: Network El Segundo opens a first-100 Tezos wallet roster for participatory art
subhead: A shared Kukai login, public counter, and zero-capital PointCast campaign begin the participant network before any sale or payout contract goes live.
disclosure: Official PointCast Press Wire filing for Network El Segundo. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
summary: Network El Segundo is recruiting its first 100 verified Tezos wallets through a free message signature while publishing the proposed art-sale participation rule and current roster count in public.
body: Network El Segundo is open as a participatory art-network prototype with a concrete first milestone: 100 verified Tezos wallet participants. A visitor can enter from PointCast, authenticate with Kukai through the shared PointCast session, and join the roster with a free message signature. No purchase, mint, wallet funding, or blockchain transaction is required to become a verified participant.

The proposed commerce rule is simple and remains explicitly pre-launch: a wallet that completes a future qualifying art purchase would join the sale-distribution list, and 50 percent of proceeds from each recorded sale would be reserved for distribution among eligible participant wallets after that sale. The current release does not deploy a sale contract, payout contract, token, or automated yield system, and it does not promise profit or a return.

The roster count is published through a public API instead of being estimated from page views. PointCast house ads route people to the same canonical entry, use page context rather than visitor profiles, and report aggregate impressions and clicks without storing wallet or visitor identifiers. The campaign uses owned PointCast inventory and no paid media.

Wallet authentication remains non-custodial. PointCast never asks for a seed phrase or private key, and the login signature does not move tez. Any later purchase, sale, or payout action would require a separate visible implementation, explicit wallet approval, and a new public verification pass before it could be described as live.

kicker: 31 WORKS · TWO SERIES · ONE TEZ · 50/50 SPLIT
headline: HOME / Art Kitty opens 31 one-tez collector editions with a built-in fund for the next work
subhead: Every collection sends half to the artist and earmarks half for future art while minting a wallet-owned edition bound to the exact published image.
disclosure: Official PointCast Press Wire filing for HOME / Art Kitty. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
summary: HOME / Art Kitty publishes 31 works across two permanent web series, each available as a one-per-wallet Tezos collector edition for one tez with an equal artist and Art Kitty proceeds split.
body: HOME / Art Kitty is now public as two web-native series containing 31 works by Michael Hoydich. Series 01 gathers 15 works from the home folder; Series 02 adds 16 bright signals moving through El Segundo, screen culture, sport, commerce, flowers, ghosts, and positive energy. Every work has its own permanent URL and exact source-image record.

Each work can be collected once per wallet for one tez through a non-custodial Kukai flow on Tezos Mainnet. The collector approves one atomic operation group: 0.5 tez to the artist, 0.5 tez earmarked for the Art Kitty, and a zero-tez mint into the collector's wallet-owned contract. The token metadata binds the edition to the published image's SHA-256 hash.

The Art Kitty is not presented as a platform fee. It is an earmarked fund for printing, tools, experiments, future images, and small grants. In this release, the artist and Art Kitty tranches use the same PointCast treasury address while remaining separately identified in the operation and token metadata; the kitty share is therefore an accounting commitment rather than a separate custodied wallet.

Publishing the site and this filing does not sign or submit a Tezos transaction. A collector must connect a wallet, review the three visible actions in Kukai, and approve the Mainnet operation. Browsing every work remains public and does not require a wallet.

kicker: 115 ROOMS · SIX HOUSE ADS · ONE SHARED PULSE

disclosure: Official PointCast product filing. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
summary: The PointCast Drum Noun Universe gathers 115 playable public rooms into one compendium, connects them through a shared browser pulse, and introduces a transparent first-party house-ad campaign across PointCast.
body: PointCast has opened the Drum Noun Universe as a public compendium of 115 browser rooms. What began as a simple drum surface now includes instruments, sequencers, short games, broadcast rooms, ritual objects, communal stages, tiny keepsakes, and agent-readable entry points. The compendium keeps those strange little rooms available instead of collapsing them into a single replacement product.

A shared browser pulse gives the collection continuity. Some rooms make sound, some keep score locally, some receive public events, and some simply offer a bell, pattern, or quiet moment. The Nouns provide an open CC0 cast for the world, while the behavior of every room remains ordinary web software that a visitor can inspect and enter directly.

The release is accompanied by a seven-creative PointCast house campaign: one featured Drum Noun Universe poster across the homepage and public network, plus six contextual Drum Compendium ads distributed across the Drum routes. Placement is chosen from the page URL rather than a visitor profile. The campaign uses no behavioral targeting, impression pixels, or paid media.

Every featured route is available without signup, wallet connection, purchase, mint, or token. No Drum token is live in this release. Wallet-backed actions elsewhere on PointCast remain explicit and separate from entering the Drum Noun Universe.

summary: Chartmaker is a browser-based lab for turning PointCast-native and public sources into daily charts, cross-source remixes, and timeline ideas.
body: PointCast Chartmaker is live as a visual source lab for data that would otherwise sit behind separate routes and feeds. It presents ten chart directions for the day, five remix prompts, and a catalog of sources that can become boards, comparisons, or timelines.

The human page is paired with /chartmaker.json so software agents can inspect the same source catalog and generated packet without scraping the interface. The related /chart and /chart.json routes continue to publish one deterministic chart of the day from the PointCast ledger.
Chartmaker is exploratory: it helps a visitor choose a useful visual treatment and inspect the ingredients. It does not present browser-local experiments or third-party sources as audited research.

body: The El Segundo School is live as a public field archive containing 652 image works organized across 163 sets. The gallery treats the archive as a school and living research surface: university ephemera, flower commons, plant study, systems, type, student life, and the visual character of El Segundo share one navigable world.

Selected works can expose optional one-tez Tezos collector editions. A published image is not automatically a minted object, and every wallet-backed step remains an explicit visitor authorization.

kicker: RF FIELD BENCH · 25-MILE LAYER · SIGNAL AUDIO
headline: RADIUS / 90245 makes a 25-mile RF link budget playable
subhead: The public engineering bench turns path loss, received power, noise, SNR, Fresnel clearance, light-time, and ideal capacity into a shareable signal study.
disclosure: Official PointCast product filing. This is an owned announcement, not independent reporting or paid client coverage.
summary: RADIUS / 90245 is a browser-based free-space RF link bench centered on El Segundo with adjustable path, antenna, noise, Fresnel, capacity, and sonification controls.
body: RADIUS / 90245 is live as a shareable radio-frequency field bench centered on El Segundo. The browser tool exposes the ingredients of a free-space link budget across a 25-mile local layer instead of hiding them behind a single pass/fail answer.

A visitor can inspect path loss, received power, noise, signal-to-noise ratio, Fresnel clearance, light-time, and ideal capacity, then optionally hear the link as signal audio. The bench is meant for learning, discussion, and early comparison—not licensed engineering sign-off.
The route belongs to the University of El Segundo's public tools layer and gives PointCast a concrete engineering product alongside its games, archives, rooms, and publishing systems.
